ca_mount_olympus.blurb: A small bolted tower in the Santa Monica Mountains, reached by a steep fire road below the Sandstone Peak area. It holds ten sport routes, running from an easy 5.7 up through a handful of 5.10s and 5.11s, with two 5.12s at the top end. The climbing is on volcanic rock studded with cobbles that serve as handholds and footholds, so it is knobby and pulling rather than crimpy. Bolts are spaced farther apart than at most sport crags, and some lines feel more committing than their numbers suggest. The tower faces north, which keeps it cooler than many of its neighbours. It suits climbers comfortable leading at their limit with a long clip.

ca_pink_wall.blurb: A pink-tinted sport wall on the main trail through Echo Cliffs in the Santa Monica Mountains, reached from the Mishe Mokwa trailhead. Ten bolted routes cover a hard-leaning spread: one at 5.10, four at 5.11, four at 5.12 and a single 5.13. The face is mostly vertical with steeper stretches, and the lines run roughly 80 to 90 feet with around nine bolts each. It picks up shade from early afternoon into evening, which helps on warm days. Expect varied movement on crimps, pockets and side pulls, and take care with holds that have broken on some routes. Best for climbers already leading in the low to mid 5.11 range.

ca_one_of_these_days_buttress.blurb: A steep buttress within Cloudburst Canyon, in the Woodfords area south of Lake Tahoe, set back from the highway and visible from it. Nine of its ten routes are trad and one is sport, so bring a rack. Difficulty spans from 5.9 to 5.13: two at 5.9, four at 5.10, one 5.11, two 5.12 and one 5.13. The wall faces north, shaded early and sunny later in the day, and the canyon holds a stream that is handy for cooling off. The short walk in makes it an easy add-on to a day in the canyon. The namesake 5.10 line is the draw, and is a good target for a confident trad leader.
ca_one_of_these_days_buttress.parking_note: A dirt pullout on the south side of Highway 88, a little west of the neighbouring Storm Trooper Buttress, serves as the car park for the canyon.

ca_overking_boulder.blurb: The one standout boulder in a small trailside sector near Castle Peak in the Donner and Truckee area, at roughly 7,500 feet. It carries ten problems, mostly moderate: about five in the V0 to V1 range, three at V2, one V3, and a single standout line around V6. The block sits right beside the path, and is sunny on one side and shaded on the other, so you can follow the conditions around it. Landings and rock quality are not well described, so scout before committing. A relaxed spot for a short session or a warm-up for harder projects elsewhere in the area, with little commitment on the walk.
ca_overking_boulder.approach: From the pullout on the dirt road, take the muddy rutted road to a meadow, skirt its left side and follow the trail west across a creek; the boulder is beside the path soon after.
